title: mail-client: emailpush feature (typed emailPush helpers, parse_push_payload)
description:
Design: docs/design/emailpush.md. Decisions: docs/design/DECISIONS.md.
Note key: E12. Crates: jmap-mail-client. Size: S.

Spec: draft-ietf-jmap-emailpush-05 §3 (clients MUST NOT rely on EmailPush as a complete record; RECOMMENDED property choice), §4, §6 (client MUST specify keys and ignore pushes not encrypted with them). Design: docs/design/emailpush.md §8; decisions 3 and 8.

In crate-jmap-mail-client add feature emailpush = ["jmap-mail-types/emailpush"] with methods/push.rs: EmailPushSubscriptionInput (a create with REQUIRED keys, so a keyless create cannot be built); set_email_push(sub_id, Option<BTreeMap<Id, EmailPushConfig>>) and patch_email_push(sub_id, account, Option<EmailPushConfig>), both over the base-client PushSubscription/set binding with JMAP_EMAILPUSH_URI in using; parse_push_payload(&[u8]) -> #[non_exhaustive] PushPayload { StateChange, PushVerification, EmailPush, Other(Value) }, which dispatches on @type over DECRYPTED bytes. Rustdoc carries the §6 MUST, the §3 MUST NOT rely, and the RECOMMENDED property ordering. No re-export of the mail-types accessors (Public API rule 6).
Acceptance: parse_push_payload on the §5 EmailPush figure and on the RFC 8620 §7.1 and §7.2.2 examples; the create input cannot omit keys (compile-time: required field); request using contains the emailpush URI. Public-api snapshot refreshed.
